setlist.title: Stuck Inside of Mobile With the Memphis Blues Again

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Tunning** (2 reviews): Phil teased Dark Star during tuning, audible about 3:30 into the recording, though the band never played it; Phil's Dark Star tease is audible during the first set tune-up [17][21]
- **Looks Like Rain** (2 reviews): Heavy rain started just as Bobby finished this song; Listener considers this probably the best 1989 version, with chest-pounding bass in parts of the stadium [19][23]
- **I Will Take You Home** (2 reviews): Big screen showed a picture of Brent's child during this song, which the listener found sweet; Brent's performance of this song stuck in the listener's memory [16][20]
- **Cold Rain and Snow** (1 review): Brent's Hammond B-3 gave this song a classic 1980s Dead sound [26]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): From the upper deck, the bass felt strong enough to collapse the stadium's upper level during this song [22]
- **To Lay Me Down** (1 review): Listener was surprised it was played and found it good for a stadium show [23]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Listener highlights He's Gone as the second set opener, a Jerry choice, paired with the prior night's Sugaree opener [21]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Listed among the listener's standouts, along with Cold Rain, Jed, Lay Me Down, Looks Like Rain and Wharf Rat [22]

## The recordings

- **gd89-07-13.schoeps.9046.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 174 min; rated 3.8/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: Bass lows come through well on this audience recording; a bit of EQ and volume helps it come alive; Audience recording has a wide, 3D stereo field, though the recording level is low [22][27]
- **gd1989-07-13.nak100.mchugh.hanscom-.32897.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 162 min; rated 2.4/5 by 5 [2]. Said about its sound: Hiss in the second set is actually steady, cold rain; the opening seconds of He's Gone are missing, with tape saturation; The last minute or so of Good Lovin' is missing from this copy [2]
- **gd1989-07-13.163770.mtx.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 172 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd1989-07-13.163771.dts.tobin.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 172 min [10]
- **gd1989-07-13.sbd.miller.95939.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 8 songs; 75 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [15]. Said about its sound: Band sounds slightly out of tune at the start; the bass is huge in the soundboard recording [26]

## Around the show

- Fans unfurled a sign reminding the band of five years without Dark Star; Phil reacted in mock surprise [17]
- Downpour began right after Looks Like Rain ended and lasted to the encore; the field turned to deep mud [19]
- Rain fell through most of the second set, clearing for the U.S. Blues encore [20]
- Rain fell at some point at nearly every show that summer; this was the last tour allowing camping at shows [24]
- Fans stayed near the river between shows; a portajohn was tipped over onto someone [24]
- Listener thinks it may not be the best of the tour, but it has its moments [23]
- Listener judged this the better of the two RFK shows, with fewer flubs than night one, whose sound took half the show to settle [26]
- Second set felt like a snoozer, with too much Drums, though well played [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd89-07-13.schoeps.9046.sbeok.shnf**: source: (Schoeps)AUD>PCM>DAT>CDR [1]. Also: Schoeps audience recording transferred via PCM and DAT to CDR; seeded to etree by Tim W [1]
- **gd1989-07-13.nak100.mchugh.hanscom-.32897.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Boyd McHugh; transferred by Dave  Hanscom; source: NAK-100s > Sony D-5, using Dolby B. [2]. Also: Shorten files were converted to FLAC using shntool; conversion credited to Gary F [2]
- **gd1989-07-13.163770.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) [4]. Also: This is a matrix mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in February 2023 [4]
- **gd1989-07-13.163771.dts.tobin.flac16**: transferred by DTS-Audio-CD 5.1 Mix by Kevin Tobin; source: DTS-Audio-CD 5.1 Mix [10]. Also: DTS surround version mixed by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in February 2023 [10]
- **gd1989-07-13.sbd.miller.95939.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> CD [15]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by michaelsmusiclog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead: “Robert F. Kennedy Stadium, Washington, D.C., July 12 & 13, 1989” (2017) CD Review](https://michaelsmusiclog.blogspot.com/2018/03/grateful-dead-robert-f-kennedy-stadium.html) [31]
- Poster by michaelsmusiclog.blogspot.com: [Grateful Dead: “Robert F. Kennedy Stadium, Washington, D.C., July 12 & 13, 1989” (2017) CD Review](https://michaelsmusiclog.blogspot.com/2018/03/grateful-dead-robert-f-kennedy-stadium.html) [32]

claims.text: Big screen showed a picture of Brent's child during this song, which the listener found sweet
Fans unfurled a sign reminding the band of five years without Dark Star; Phil reacted in mock surprise
Phil teased Dark Star during tuning, audible about 3:30 into the recording, though the band never played it
Downpour began right after Looks Like Rain ended and lasted to the encore; the field turned to deep mud
Heavy rain started just as Bobby finished this song
Rain fell through most of the second set, clearing for the U.S. Blues encore
Brent's performance of this song stuck in the listener's memory
Listener highlights He's Gone as the second set opener, a Jerry choice, paired with the prior night's Sugaree opener
Phil's Dark Star tease is audible during the first set tune-up
From the upper deck, the bass felt strong enough to collapse the stadium's upper level during this song
Bass lows come through well on this audience recording; a bit of EQ and volume helps it come alive
Listed among the listener's standouts, along with Cold Rain, Jed, Lay Me Down, Looks Like Rain and Wharf Rat
Listener considers this probably the best 1989 version, with chest-pounding bass in parts of the stadium
Listener was surprised it was played and found it good for a stadium show
Listener thinks it may not be the best of the tour, but it has its moments
Rain fell at some point at nearly every show that summer; this was the last tour allowing camping at shows
Fans stayed near the river between shows; a portajohn was tipped over onto someone
Listener judged this the better of the two RFK shows, with fewer flubs than night one, whose sound took half the show to settle
Brent's Hammond B-3 gave this song a classic 1980s Dead sound
Band sounds slightly out of tune at the start; the bass is huge in the soundboard recording
Audience recording has a wide, 3D stereo field, though the recording level is low
Listener says this version rocks
Second set felt like a snoozer, with too much Drums, though well played
Schoeps audience recording transferred via PCM and DAT to CDR; seeded to etree by Tim W
Shorten files were converted to FLAC using shntool; conversion credited to Gary F
Hiss in the second set is actually steady, cold rain; the opening seconds of He's Gone are missing, with tape saturation
The last minute or so of Good Lovin' is missing from this copy
This is a matrix mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in February 2023
